title: Music icon Molly Meldrum dies
transcript:
Speaker 1: This is Gabriella Power with your News 24 update. Molly Meldrum has died in Melbourne after a long battle with ill health. The Herald Sun says the music guru died this morning in hospital. He is being remembered as a champion of Aussie musicians after his successful stint hosting Countdown between 1974 and 1983. A nest of red imported fire ants found in suburban Sydney has been destroyed. The New South Wales government confirmed the discovery of a nest in Auburn and testing shows it could have been there for up to 12 months. It's not known if it's linked to the nest previously found about six kilometres away in Enfield. The government urges the public to report any suspicious earth mounds but not to attempt to disrupt or destroy any suspected ant nests. For the first time, Angus Taylor has taken the lead as preferred Prime Minister in the latest poll. The news poll in The Australian shows the opposition leader leading Anthony Albanese 42 to 41%. The Prime Minister's net approval rating has dropped to a record low. 64% of voters are dissatisfied with his performance and 33% are satisfied. Labor and One Nation are leading the primary vote, tied at 27% each, but core support for the coalition has risen for the fourth time to 22%.
Speaker 2: Anthony Albanese hasn't delivered on his promise to make sure that no Australian is left behind. At a time when inflation's going up and interest rates are going up and now unemployment is going up as well, clearly Labor's economic model is not working and that's beginning to play out in the polls.
Speaker 1: The reinstatement of ticking the box to add organ donation to Queensland drivers' licences has done wonders for the register. More than 4,000 people have been added since the change. Queensland now joins South Australia as the only state with organ donation tied to licence applications. The Festival State has the highest rate of registered donors at 74%. The US Army will detonate nearly five tonnes of toxic lead aside at an Iowa munitions plant over the next few days. A federal appeals court paused the Army's permit to prevent the move, but the Trump administration says they have invoked emergency powers to allow the Army to act without one. The Army says the degraded material could explode on its own or drop in temperature, could destabilise the material and lead to an uncontrolled explosion. Environmental groups argue the controlled explosion would release a toxic plume of lead dusts into the air that could travel up to 160 kilometres, exposing surrounding communities. Those airlines' flights are delayed across the United States due to a system-wide outage of a program used to calculate aircraft weights and safety settings. The airline says teams are working to restore automation for departing flight weight and balance calculations, but is currently using manual workarounds to get flights moving. These pre-departure checks are crucial to ensuring aircraft can fly safely. It's the busiest week of the year for travel across America ahead of Thanksgiving weekend. Rescue workers have recovered 24 bodies after a massive fire swept through a candy factory in Indonesia. Fifteen people survived the blaze in western Java. Four of them have been taken to hospital. Rescuers are searching for dozens of other missing factory workers. It took more than 12 hours for firefighters to contain the blaze.
